nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:DAS}
   In the setting from above, we define the following concepts:
   \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
      \item \hypertarget{converge}A sequence $\seq{u}$, $u_n \in X_n$, is said to \emph{converge} to $u \in X$, if $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \Vert p_n u - u_n \Vert_{X_n} = 0$. 
      \item \hypertarget{compactseq}A sequence $\seq{u}$, $u_n \in X_n$, is called \emph{compact}, if for every subsequence $\mathbb{N}' \subset \mathbb{N}$ there exists a subsubsequence $\mathbb{N}'' \subset \mathbb{N}'$ and $u \in X$ such that $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}''}$ converges to $u$.
      \item \hypertarget{approximate}A sequence of operators $\seq{A}$, $A_n \in L(X_n)$, \emph{approximates} (also called \emph{asymptotic consistency}) an operator $A \in L(X)$, if $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \Vert A_n p_n u - p_n A u \Vert_{X_n} = 0$ for all $u \in X$.
      \item \hypertarget{compactop}A sequence of operators $\seq{A}$, $A_n \in L(X_n)$, is called \emph{compact}, if for every bounded sequence $\seq{u}$, $u_n \in X_n$, $\Vert u_n \Vert_{X_n} \le C$, the sequence $\seq{A_n u}$ is compact.
      \item \hypertarget{stable}A sequence of operators $\seq{A}$, $A_n \in L(X_n)$, is called \emph{stable}, if there exist constants $C > 0$, $n_0 > 0$, such that $A_n$ is invertible and $\Vert A_n^{-1} \Vert_{L(X_n)} \le C$ for all $n > n_0$. 
      \item \hypertarget{regular}A sequence of operators $\seq{A}$, $A_n \in L(X_n)$, is said to be \emph{regular}, if $\Vert u_n \Vert_{X_n} \le C$ and the compactness of $\seq{A_n u}$ imply the compactness of $\seq{u}$ itself.
   \end{enumerate} 
   \hypertarget{DAS}We call the triple $(X_n,p_n,A_n)$ a \emph{discrete approximation scheme} (DAS) of $(X,A)$ if we have that $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \Vert p_n u \Vert_{X_n} = \Vert u \Vert_X$ for all $u \in X$ and $A_n$ approximates $A$.

nodes.statement: As discussed above, we may choose X_T_n as the Brezzi-Douglas-Marini (BDM) space defined as X_T_n coloneqq BDM_k coloneqq \ u_tau in [P^k(T_n)]^d : jumpu_tau cdot boldsymbolnu_F = 0 \ forall F in F_n \ subset H(div, O), where we recall that jumpcdot_F, F in F_n, denotes the usual DG-jump operator. To obtain an H(div)-conforming HDG discretization , we set X_F_n to be the space of tangential polynomials on the skeleton F_n: X_F_n coloneqq P^k,tang(F_n) = \ u_F in [P^k(F_n)]^d : P_boldsymbolnu u_F = 0 \. For these choices, we redefine the HDG-jump operators as hdgjumpu_n coloneqq P_boldsymbolnu^perp u_tau - u_F such that hdgjumpu_n_boldsymbolnu = 0. Consequently, we obtain that R^l u_n = 0 for all u_n in X_n and therefore we have that div_boldsymbolnu^n = div and s_n(cdot,cdot) = 0. To optimize the computational efficiency, we can use relaxed H(div)-conforming spaces as introduced in . We define BDM_k^- coloneqq \ u_tau in [P^k(T_n)]^d : Pi_F^k-1 jumpu_tau cdot boldsymbolnu_F = 0 \ forall F in F_n \, where Pi_F^k-1 is the L^2-projection onto [P^k-1(F)]^d. While functions in BDM_k^- are not normal-continuous in the highest order, this relaxation reduces the number of coupling degrees of freedoms improving the sparsity pattern of the system matrices. The choice of X_T_n = BDM_k^- and X_F_n = P^k,tang(F_n) still yields R^l u_n = 0 if the lifting degree satisfies l le k-1.

\label{lem:weakConvergence}
   Let $\seq{\mathbf{u}} \subset \mathbb{X}_n$ be such that $\sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \Vert \mathbf{u}_n \Vert_{\mathbb{X}_n} < \infty$. Then there exists $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{X}$ and a subsequence $\mathbb{N}' \subset \mathbb{N}$ such that $\PVol{\mathbf{u}_n} \overset{\mathbf{L}^2}{\rightharpoonup} \mathbf{u}$, $c_s^2 \rho \operatorname{div}_{\boldsymbol{\nu}}^n \mathbf{u}_n \overset{L^2}{\rightharpoonup} c_s^2 \rho \operatorname{div} \mathbf{u}$ and $\rho \mathbf{D}_{\mathbf{b}}^n \mathbf{u}_n \overset{\mathbf{L}^2}{\rightharpoonup} \rho \partial_{\mathbf{b}} \mathbf{u}$, $n \in \mathbb{N}'$.

nodes.statement: We modify standard arguments from the DG-case, see e.g. and , to the HDG setting, see also . \\ By assumption, the sequences PVolu_n, rho D_b^n u_n and c_s^2 rho div_boldsymbolnu^n u_n are bounded in L^2 and L^2, respectively. Thus, there exist a subsequence N' subset N and elements u, bmg in L^2, q in L^2 such that PVolu_n oversetL^2rightharpoonup u, c_s^2 rho div_boldsymbolnu^n u_n oversetL^2rightharpoonup q and rho D_b^n u_n oversetL^2rightharpoonup bmg. It remains to show that bmg = rho partial_b u and q = c_s^2 rho div u. We only show the former, as the latter follows with a similar argumentation for the scalar lifting operator R^l, see also . Let bmpsi in bmC^infty_0 and bmpsi_n be the lowest order standard mathbf H^1-interpolant of bmpsi on T_n. Then, we compute with element-wise partial integration - inner&PVolu_n, rho partial_b bmpsi_T_n \\ &= innerrpartial_b PVolu_n, bmpsi_T_n - innerr(b cdot boldsymbolnu) PVolu_n, bmpsi_partial T_n + underbraceinnerr(b cdot boldsymbolnu) PFacu_n, bmpsi_partial T_n_=0 \\[-0.25cm] &= innerrpartial_b PVolu_n, bmpsi_T_n - innerrhdgjumpu_n_b, bmpsi_partial T_n \\ overset&= innerrpartial_b PVolu_n, bmpsi_T_n - innerrhdgjumpu_n_b, bmpsi - bmpsi_n_partial T_n + innerrR^\!l u_n, bmpsi_n_T_n \\ overset&= innerrpartial_b PVolu_n, bmpsi - bmpsi_n_T_n - innerrhdgjumpu_n_b, bmpsi - bmpsi_n_partial T_n + innerrD_b^n u_n, bmpsi_n_T_n \\ &= -innerPVolu_n, rho partial_b left( bmpsi-bmpsi_n right)_T_n + innerrD_b^n u_n, bmpsi_n_T_n, where we recall that div(rho b) = 0 by assumption. Since Vert bmpsi - bmpsi_n Vert_mathbf H^1 lesssim h_n Vert bmpsi Vert_mathbf H^2 and Vert u_n Vert_X_n lesssim 1, it follows that lim_n to infty innerrD_b^n u_n, bmpsi_n_T_n = lim_n to infty - innerPVolu_n, rho partial_b bmpsi_n_T_n. Thus, we obtain innerbmg, bmpsi &= lim_n rightarrow infty innerrD_b^n u_n, bmpsi = lim_n to infty left( innerrD_b^n u_n, bmpsi - bmpsi_n_T_n + innerrD_b^n u_n, bmpsi_n_T_n right) \\ overset&= lim_n rightarrow infty - innerPVolu_n, rho partial_b bmpsi_T_n = - inneru, rho partial_b bmpsi_T_n. Consequently, it holds that bmg = rho partial_b u and with similar arguments q = c_s^2 rho div u.

   The operator $A_n \in L(\mathbb{X}_n)$ \hyperlink{approximate}{approximates}~the operator $A \in L(\mathbb{X})$, i.e.~for each $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{X}$, it holds that $$\lim_{n \to \infty} \Vert (A_n p_n - p_n A) \mathbf{u} \Vert_{\mathbb{X}_n} = 0.$$

nodes.statement: In the construction above, the normal jump is attributed to w_n and the T_n-operator flips its sign. Alternatively, we can isolate the normal jump through a suitably defined lifting operator, cf.. In this case, we would decompose u_n = v_n + w_n + z_n with v_n as above and hdgjumpu_n_boldsymbolnu = hdgjumpz_n_boldsymbolnu. This construction is more natural, because since we associate w_n with the divergence free part of the Helmholtz decomposition, we would expect the normal jump to be zero. When defining T_n, we now have explicit control over the sign of the normal jump. The previous construction corresponds to T_n u_n coloneqq v_n - w_n - z_n, but we could also define T_n u_n coloneqq v_n - w_n + z_n. Note that for the latter construction, the stabilization term s_n(cdot,cdot) would have to be redefined to have a positive sign in front of the normal contribution and in the forthcoming analysis, the stabilization parameter alpha would have to be chosen sufficiently large to ensure that s_n(cdot,cdot) is positive definite. To avoid further technicalities, we do not further consider this alternative decomposition.

In the construction above, the normal jump is attributed to $\mathbf{w}_n$ and the $T_n$-operator flips its sign. Alternatively, we can isolate the normal jump through a suitably defined lifting operator, cf.~\cite{AHLS22,Thesis_vB23}. In this case, we would decompose $\mathbf{u}_n = \mathbf{v}_n + \mathbf{w}_n + \mathbf{z}_n$ with $\mathbf{v}_n$ as above and $\hdgjump{\mathbf{u}_n}_{\boldsymbol{\nu}} = \hdgjump{\mathbf{z}_n}_{\boldsymbol{\nu}}$. This construction is more natural, because since we associate $\mathbf{w}_n$ with the \emph{divergence free} part of the Helmholtz decomposition, we would expect the normal jump to be zero.  
   When defining $T_n$, we now have explicit control over the sign of the normal jump. The previous construction corresponds to $T_n \mathbf{u}_n \coloneqq \mathbf{v}_n - \mathbf{w}_n - \mathbf{z}_n$, but we could also define $T_n \mathbf{u}_n \coloneqq \mathbf{v}_n - \mathbf{w}_n + \mathbf{z}_n$. Note that for the latter construction, the stabilization term $s_n(\cdot,\cdot)$ would have to be redefined to have a positive sign in front of the normal contribution and in the forthcoming analysis, the stabilization parameter $\alpha$ would have to be chosen sufficiently large to ensure that $s_n(\cdot,\cdot)$ is positive definite. To avoid further technicalities, we do not further consider this alternative decomposition.

Due to the properties of underlinetildepi_n^d discussed in creflem:pinXd:properties, we obtain for P_V_n = underlinetildepi_n^d S_n that div_boldsymbolnu^n P_V_n u_n = div PVolP_V_n u_n = div pi_n^d nabla tildev. Using the commutation property pi_n^l div = div pi_n^d, we calculate div pi_n^d nabla tildev &= pi_n^l div nabla tildev \\ overset&= pi_n^l left( - (P_L^2_0 q cdot + M) nabla tildev + (div_boldsymbolnu^n + pi_n^l P_L^2_0 q cdot \! + M_n) u_n right) \\ &= - (P_L^2_0 q cdot + M) nabla tildev + (div_boldsymbolnu^n + pi_n^l P_L^2_0 q cdot \! + M_n) u_n \\ & + (id - pi_n^l)(P_L^2_0 q cdot + M) nabla tildev + (pi_n^l - id)M_n u_n \\ overset&= div nabla tildev + (id - pi_n^l)(P_L^2_0 q cdot + M) S_n u_n + (pi_n^l - id) M_n u_n \\ &=: div nabla tildev + hatO_n u_n. Thus, we have that Vert c_s rho^1/2 div_boldsymbolnu^n P_V_n u_n Vert^2_T_n &= langle c_s^2 rho div pi_n^d nabla tildev, div pi_n^d nabla tildev rangle \\ &= langle c_s^2 rho div nabla tildev, div nabla tildev rangle + langle checkO_n u_n, u_n rangle_X_n, where we define the operator checkO_n through langle checkO_n u_n, u_n' rangle_X_n coloneqq &langle c_s^2 rho div pi_n^d nabla tildev, hatO_n u_n' rangle + langle c_s^2 rho hatO_n u_n, div (pi_n^d nabla tildev)' rangle \\ &+ langle c_s^2 rho hatO_n u_n, hatO_n u_n' rangle. With similar arguments as in creflem:PvIdempotent, we can show lim_n to infty Vert hatO_n Vert_L(X_n,L^2_0) = 0 and thus lim_n to infty Vert checkO_n Vert_L(X_n) = 0. In the following, we use similar techniques as in the proof of to show that the first term can be estimated suitably by a weighted mathbf H^1-seminorm. By assumption, O is a convex Lipschitz polyhedron and thus, we can apply to estimate for any v in mathbf H^1_boldsymbolnu 0 Vert div (v) Vert^2_L^2 \! = \! \! \! sum_i,j = 1^d langle partial_x_j v_i, partial_x_i v_j rangle_L^2 \! - \! \! int_partial O \! \! \! \! B(P_boldsymbolnu^perp v, P_boldsymbolnu^perp v) ds ge \! \! \! sum_i,j = 1^d langle partial_x_j v_i, partial_x_i v_j rangle_L^2. where B(bmtau,bmtau') := -partial_bmtau boldsymbolnu cdot overlinebmtau' is the second fundamental quadratic form of partial O applied to tangential vector fields bmtau,bmtau' and partial_bmtau is the tangential derivative. \label{thm:convergence}
   Assume that \cref{assumption:MachNumber} holds. For $\mathbf{f} \in \mathbf{L}^2$, let $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{X}$ be the solution to \eqref{eq:cont:weakForm}. Then, there exists an index $n_0 > 0$ such that for all $n > n_0$ the problem \eqref{eq:discr:weakForm} has a unique solution $\mathbf{u}_n \in \mathbb{X}_n$ and $\lim_{n \to \infty} d_n(\mathbf{u},\mathbf{u}_n) = 0$.

nodes.statement: To show the convergence rate, we continue to estimate . For the first term, creflem:pinXRates yields that d_n(u,underlinepi_n u) lesssim h_n^min\1+s,k\. For the second term, we note that Vert p_n u - u_n Vert_X_n le ( sup_n > n_0 Vert A_n^-1 Vert_L(X_n)) Vert A_n(p_n u - u_n) Vert_X_n and compute with similar arguments as in crefthm:AnToA that Vert A_n &(p_n u - u_n) Vert_X_n = sup_u_n' in X_n Vert u_n' Vert_X_n = 1 vert a_n(p_n u - u_n, u_n') vert \\ &le C d_n(u,p_n u) + sup_u_n' in X_n Vert u_n' Vert_X_n = 1 vert langle c_s^2 rho div u, div_boldsymbolnu^n u_n' rangle \\ & - langle rho (omega+ipartial_b+iOmegatimes) u, (omega+iD_b^n+iOmegatimes) u_n' rangle \\ & + langle div u, nabla p cdot u_n' rangle + langle nabla p cdot u, div_boldsymbolnu^n u_n' rangle + langle (Hess(p) - rho Hess(phi)) u, u_n' rangle \\ & - i omega langle gamma rho u, u_n' rangle - langle f, u_n' rangle vert. For the first term, we again use the estimates from creflem:pnBoundedBypinX and creflem:pinXRates. For the remainder, we want to integrate by parts and use the fact that u solves . This requires that u in mathbf H^2 is regular enough, because a right hand-side f in L^2 only grants -nabla(c_s^2 rho div u) + rho partial_b partial_b u which however does not imply that -nabla(c_s^2 rho div u) in L^2 or rho partial_b partial_b u in L^2. Let bmpsi_n in [P^l(T_n)]^d be a suitable H^1-projection of (omega+ipartial_b+iOmegatimes) u, for example as in . Then, we have that langle (omega+ipartial_b+iOmegatimes) u, rho D_b^n u_n' rangle = langle bmpsi_n, rho D_b^n u_n' rangle + langle (omega+ipartial_b+iOmegatimes) u - bmpsi_n, rho D_b^n u_n' rangle, and similar to we calculate with the definition and div(rho b) = 0 that langle bmpsi_n, &rho D_b^n u_n' rangle = langle bmpsi_n, rho partial_b u_tau' rangle_T_n + langle bmpsi_n, rho R^\!l u_n' rangle_T_n \\ &= - langle rho partial_b bmpsi_n, u_tau' rangle_T_n + langle bmpsi_n, rho hdgjumpu_n'_b rangle_partial T_n + langle bmpsi_n, rho R^\!l u_n' rangle_T_n \\ &= - langle rho partial_b (omega+ipartial_b+iOmegatimes) u, u_tau' rangle_T_n + langle rho partial_b ((omega+ipartial_b+iOmegatimes) u - bmpsi_n), u_tau' rangle_T_n. Altogether, we obtain that sup_u_n' in X_n Vert u_n' Vert_X_n = 1 &vert langle c_s^2 rho div u, div_boldsymbolnu^n u_n' rangle - langle rho (omega+ipartial_b+iOmegatimes) u, (omega+iD_b^n+iOmegatimes) u_n' rangle \\ &\ + langle div u, nabla p cdot u_n' rangle \! + \! langle nabla p cdot u, div_boldsymbolnu^n u_n' rangle \! + \! langle (Hess(p) - rho Hess(phi)) u, u_n' rangle \\ &\ - i omega langle gamma rho u, u_n' rangle - langle f, u_n' rangle vert \\ &lesssim Vert rho (omega+ipartial_b+iOmegatimes) u - bmpsi_n Vert_mathbf H^1 + Vert c_s^2 rho div u - psi_n Vert_H^1 \\ &\ + Vert nabla p cdot u - tildepsi_n Vert_H^1 \\ &lesssim h^min\ l,s\. Combining all estimates, we obtain the desired result.

nodes.name: The case $l = k-1$
nodes.statement: While the convergence estimate in crefthm:convEstimates suggest the choice l = k for the degree of the lifting operator R^\!l, the numerical experiments in crefsubsec:numex:conv suggest that the choice l = k-1 (together with a reduced facet space X_F_n = P^k-1(F_n)) might be sufficient to obtain optimal convergence rates. Thus, it might be possible to improve the results presented in crefthm:convEstimates to obtain the estimate d_n(u,u_n) lesssim h_n^min\s,k,l+1\.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{rem:CA:improvement}
   While the convergence estimate in \cref{thm:convEstimates} suggest the choice $l = k$ for the degree of the lifting operator $\mathbf{R}^{\!l}$, the numerical experiments in \cref{subsec:numex:conv} suggest that the choice $l = k-1$ (together with a reduced facet space $\mathbb{X}_{\mathcal{F}_n} = \mathbb{P}^{k-1}(\mathcal{F}_n)$) might be sufficient to obtain optimal convergence rates. Thus, it might be possible to improve the results presented in \cref{thm:convEstimates} to obtain the estimate $d_n(\mathbf{u},\mathbf{u}_n) \lesssim h_n^{\min\{s,k,l+1\}}$.

nodes.name: Implementation of the lifting operator
nodes.statement: In practice, we implement the lifting operator R^\!l through a mixed formulation adding an auxiliary equation and variable. For all u_n, u_n' in X_n, we need to form langle rho D_b^n u_n, D_b^n u_n' rangle_T_n = &langle rho partial_b u_n, partial_b u_n' rangle_T_n + langle rho R^\!l u_n, partial_b u_n' rangle_T_n + langle rho partial_b u_n, R^\!l u_n' rangle_T_n \\ &+ langle rho R^\!l u_n, R^\!l u_n' rangle_T_n. For the mixed terms, we obtain by definition that langle rho R^\!l u_n, partial_b u_n' rangle_T_n \!+\! langle rhopartial_b u_n, R^\!l u_n' rangle_T_n \!=\! - langlerho hdgjumpu_n_b, partial_b u_n' rangle_partial T_n \!- langle rho partial_b u_n, hdgjumpu_n'_b rangle_partial T_n\!.\! For the remaining term, we introduce an auxiliary variable bmr = R^\!l u_n in [P^l(T_n)]^d with the defining that bmr fulfills langle rho bmr, bms rangle_T_n = - langle rho hdgjumpu_n_b, bms rangle_partial T_n for all bms in [P^l(T_n)]^d. Then, we have langle rho R^\!l u_n, R^\!l u_n' rangle_T_n = langle rho bmr, R^\!l u_n' rangle_T_n = overlinelangle rho R^\!l u_n', bmr rangle_T_n = - langle rho bmr, hdgjumpu_n'_b rangle_partial T_n, Thus, we can implement the term through a mixed formulation with the auxiliary variable bmr (and corresponding test function bms). As discussed in crefsubsec:method:discretization the scalar lifting operator R^l is only introduced for notational convenience in the analysis and by definition of the stabilization term s_n, we are considering a SIP method for the diffusion term. Thus, we do not have to implement the scalar lifting operator R^l explicitly.

nodes.name: Computational costs associated with the lifting operator
nodes.statement: In a DG setting, the implementation of lifting operators is usually associated with higher computational costs in the resulting linear systems because the lifting operator introduces new, less local couplings compared to classical SIP operators. In contrast, the support of the HDG-lifting operator is local since the volume unknowns only couple through the facet unknowns indirectly. Note that especially bmr and bms in crefrem:numex:liftingImpl only occur locally on each element and can be eliminated locally. Thus, in an HDG setting, the implementation of the lifting operators leads to similar computational costs than the implementation of a corresponding SIP variant. To visualize the associated computational costs, we consider the sparsity pattern of the respective system matrices in creffig:sparsitypattern. [!htbp] [scale=0.89] node (A1) at (-6,0) includegraphics[width=0.21textwidth,keepaspectratio]figures/sparsitypattern_HdivDG.png; node (B1)at (-2,0) includegraphics[width=0.21textwidth,keepaspectratio]figures/sparsitypattern_HdivSIPDG.png; node (C1) at (2,0) includegraphics[width=0.21textwidth,keepaspectratio]figures/sparsitypattern_HdivHDG.png; node (D1) at (6,0) includegraphics[width=0.21textwidth,keepaspectratio]figures/sparsitypattern_HdivSIPHDG.png; node[below=0.15cm of A1] (A) footnotesize H(div)-DG+Lift; node[below =0.1cm of A] footnotesize nzes:\ 235,036; node[below=0.15cm of B1] (B) footnotesize H(div)-DG+SIP; node[below =0.1cm of B] footnotesize nzes:\ 133,652; node[below=0.15cm of C1] (C) footnotesize H(div)-HDG+Lift; node[below =0.1cm of C] footnotesize nzes:\ 30,096; node[below=0.15cm of D1] (D) footnotesize H(div)-HDG+SIP; node[below =0.1cm of D] footnotesize nzes:\ 30,096; captionWe compare the sparsity pattern of the stiffness matrix obtained with the following four methods: H(div)-conforming DG with lifting stabilization (left), H(div)-conforming DG with SIP (middle-left), H(div)-conforming HDG with lifting stabilization (middle-right), and H(div)-conforming HDG with SIP (right). For the HDG methods, we use static condensation and for the DG method with the lifting operator, we apply the Schur complement to eliminate the unknowns associated with the lifting operator. In the HDG setting, both methods lead to the same number of non-zero entries (nzes) (even though the couplings differ slightly), whereas in the DG setting, the lifting operator almost doubles the number of non-zero entries. For the computations, we chose a mesh with 27 elements and the polynomial degree k = 5.
